absent: Locking, concurrency, allocation lifetime and validation rules for the described attributes and rings.
Netlink message handling, privilege checks, and error paths for virtual function, port, stats, program attach, tunnel and switch operations.
Socket call semantics, ring memory mapping lifecycle, fanout grouping behavior and timestamp generation details.
Virtual LAN device creation, priority mapping and flag effects beyond command and layout names.
Numeric values of enumerations and exact field widths beyond prose categories, and any entry point addresses.

findings.text: Virtual function netlink groupings cover outer info containers, per function controls for addressing and tagging and rates and spoof control and link administration and counters and trust and identifiers, plus nested tag detail and counter selectors. Each grouping ends in a private maximum sentinel with a public maximum one less.

Virtual function payloads pair a function index with one setting. Address payloads carry a wide fixed hardware address area. Tag payloads carry identifier and priority, with an extended form adding protocol in network order. Rate payloads carry one ceiling or a floor plus ceiling. Remaining payloads carry a single administrative value for spoof, link, RSS query, trust, or a wide globally unique value.

Port controls provide a nested virtual port container and attributes for owning function, profile name, virtual station identity, instance and host identity, plus numeric request input and numeric response output. Associated limits bound profile text and identity binary size and reserve a negative value meaning self. Request codes progress through pre association variants toward association and disassociation, while response codes distinguish success, format, resource, identifier, version, sync and profile lifecycle outcomes.

Virtual station identity is an eight octet layout with manager, three octet type, version, then explicit padding. Stats query header carries address family, padding, interface index and a caller supplied selection mask.

Special link families expose small attribute sets. One covers partition key, operating mode and multicast handling with datagram versus connected modes. Another covers two slaves, multicast detail, supervision address, sequence, version, protocol selector and interlink, with protocol offering two high availability variants.

Statistics retrieval defines link counter groups, extended per type counters, slave counters, offload counters and address family detail, plus get and set controls for filters and layer three offload accounting. Extended counters distinguish bridge and bond types. Offload detail distinguishes processor hit counters, hardware capability reporting with request and used flags, and hardware layer three counters. A helper maps an attribute number to a single selection bit.

Packet program attachment uses single bit update and replace controls and three mutually considered execution modes with combined mode and overall masks. Attachment state distinguishes none, single mode variants and multiple simultaneous attachments. Related attributes carry file descriptors, attachment state, flags, program identifiers per mode and expected descriptor for safe replacement. A separate event set reports reboot, feature, failover, peer notification, multicast resend and bonding option changes.

Remaining link families each expose a compact attribute set with a maximum sentinel. Tunnel controls cover ownership, type, header handling, persistence and queue counts. Cellular framing controls cover multiplex identifier and a flags word with separate ingress aggregation, command and checksum version controls for both directions. Other families cover message transport network and binding, switch conduit with a deprecated alias equal to the current name, and overlay mode with point to point versus multipoint choice.

Legacy packet address pairs family with a short device name area and network order protocol. Link layer address carries family, protocol, interface index, hardware type, packet class, hardware length and an eight octet address area.

Packet socket interface defines destination classes from local delivery through broadcast and multicast to foreign, outgoing, looped and user or kernel handling, socket options for rings and counters and thresholds and metadata and versioning and filtering and fanout and offload bypass and loss handling, fanout disciplines for hashing and balancing and processor affinity and rollover and random and queue mapping and filter driven selection with rollover and identity and direction and reassembly modifiers, and membership classes for group and promiscuous and all group and unicast capture.

Ring accounting structures count received versus dropped frames, with an extended form adding frozen queue depth and a wide rollover account distinguishing all and huge and failed events under a versioned union. Auxiliary per frame metadata carries status, lengths, offsets and tag fields. Setup structures describe block and frame geometry, with a newer form adding retire timeout, private area size and requested features under a versioned union.

Ring status words use low bits for ownership and copy and loss and checksum readiness and tag validity and timeout and format and offload protocol, and high bits for software versus hardware timestamp source. Transmit direction uses available versus requested versus sending versus format error. A feature word requests receive hash filling. Alignment is sixteen with helpers deriving header plus link address lengths per ring version across three enumerated generations.

Versioned frame headers grow from coarse seconds and microseconds plus offsets, to nanosecond timing with inline tag and padding, to chained variable layout with next offset, timing, lengths, status, offsets, a variant carrying hash and tag, and trailing padding. Block headers carry status, packet count, first packet offset, valid length, sequence and first versus last packet stamps with microsecond or nanosecond union, wrapped in a versioned union and descriptor with version and private offset. Membership requests carry interface, type, address length and address area. Fanout arguments carry identifier, discipline plus flags and member limit with field order dependent on byte order.

Virtual LAN management defines commands to add and remove devices and to set or query ingress and egress priority mapping, naming policy, flags, underlying device and identifier. Flags control header reordering, registration protocols, loose versus strict binding and bridge association. Naming policies combine raw versus symbolic base with padded versus unpadded identifier suffix and a highest sentinel.

Virtual LAN control block carries a command, a fixed primary device name area, a union second operand that may hold another name area or identifier or priority or policy or binding or flag value, and a quality field. Widths are fixed and the union overlays all alternative operands.

Public maxima equal private sentinels minus one. Filter selection shifts by attribute minus one. Tag identifiers stay within a small bounded range where zero disables filtering. Hardware address areas and device name areas and profile and identity fields have fixed capacities. Frame and block headers are padded to sixteen octet alignment. One hardware timestamp variant is marked deprecated and never set.

Administrative link control selects automatic follow versus forced up versus forced down. Port lifecycle moves from pre association through association to disassociation with success and retry and error responses. Program attachment moves among none, single mode and multiple modes under conditional create and replace semantics. Ring ownership alternates between kernel and user with copy, loss, timeout and error side states, and block retirement is driven by packet count or timeout with monotonic first and last stamps.

Callers must respect fixed capacities for addresses, names, profiles, identities and tag lists, including a tag list capacity of one. Unions overlay unrelated operands and timestamp resolutions, so readers must select by version or command. One switch attribute name is a deprecated alias of another. One timestamp source bit must not be relied upon. Endian sensitive fanout layout and network order protocol and tag protocol fields require conversion.

This lane exposes only userspace header surface: include guards, netlink attribute enumerations, flag bits, and passive payload layouts for link, packet and virtual LAN management. No kernel functions, variables, locks or callbacks are defined here.
